hypothesis: For at least one predeclared grid cell, reducing task interaction cost improves per-task interaction cost but peer-mediated adoption raises shared-verifier p95 completion latency versus frozen adoption; no-imitation and nonbinding/partitioned controls remove the reversal.

model.opportunity_denominator: every principal-tick; skipped, queued, completed, and unfinished opportunities are retained
model.percentile: nearest-rank p95 over all generated task completion latencies; null if no completed task
model.randomness: stdlib random.Random initialized independently by frozen seed and deterministic mode/topology-derived seed offsets

decision.reversal: reduced_peer p95 > reduced_frozen p95 for the same topology/seed/imitation/capacity cell, with lower per-task interaction cost (6 < 10)
decision.negative_controls: at matching grid settings, the reversal count for imitation=0, server_count=24, and server_count=3 must each be zero
decision.pass: at least one preregistered contiguous peer-imitation/capacity region (imitation 0.08 and 0.2 at server_count 1) has a reversal for both topologies and at least 3/4 seeds per cell, while all three negative controls have zero reversals
decision.no_reversal: no grid cell meets the scoped reversal condition
decision.scope: synthetic mechanism/sensitivity only; no empirical adoption, task elasticity, capacity, runtime, user, or product inference
